description: FlashML flashlib supplies the tuned GPU DBSCAN reference whose geomean sets this task's score cap. The repository holds dbscanlib, a small torch package with a naive, correct dbscan entry point. The agent submits a patch at /app/solution.patch that may rewrite Python files or add Triton kernels under dbscanlib/ only. The judge runs held-out low-cluster-count point sets with D at least 8 on a Modal H100 and gates every timed iteration on an Adjusted Rand Index of 0.99. Score is 100 times log geomean speedup over log of the 130x target in config.yaml, with the reference near 65x.

FlashML flashlib supplies the GEMM-based IVF-PQ search reference that anchors this task's scoring. The repository holds ivfpqlib, a torch package exposing ivf_pq_search over a prebuilt inverted-file product-quantization index. The agent submits a patch at /app/solution.patch touching only Python files under ivfpqlib/, Triton included. The judge times the search alone on SIFT workloads with nlist 8192 on a Modal H100, hands each call a fresh index copy, and gates on iso-result recall@k of 0.99 against the full-nprobe baseline. Score is 100 times log geomean speedup over log of the 2551x target in config.yaml, twice the pinned reference of 1276x.

FlashML flashlib supplies the GPU k-means reference kernels from which this task's score cap derives. The repository holds kmeanslib, whose step entry point performs one Lloyd iteration on bfloat16 data and returns full labels plus updated centroids. The agent submits a patch at /app/solution.patch that changes only Python files under kmeanslib/. The judge owns the iteration loop, runs hidden workloads on a Modal H100, and gates on returned inertia within 5 percent of the baseline plus a 0.002 label-mismatch fraction. Score is 100 times log geomean speedup over log of the 20x target in config.yaml, twice the fused best-known 9.97x.

FlashML flashlib supplies the brute-force GPU k-NN reference whose geomean sets this task's cap. The repository holds knnlib, whose knn entry point returns squared-L2 distances and indices over bfloat16 inputs. The agent submits a patch at /app/solution.patch restricted to Python files under knnlib/, Triton allowed. The judge draws fresh random query and database subsets of SIFT and GIST descriptors on every timed iteration on a Modal H100 and gates on ball-recall of 0.88 against exact fp32 distances. Score is 100 times log geomean speedup over log of the 4x target in config.yaml, twice the reference 1.94x.

The task is an original cryptanalysis challenge rather than a paper reproduction. The repository ships a public catalog of 200 structured-LWE instances across ten families, a read-only Python facade at /app/public/lwe_instance.py that reconstructs A from a SHAKE-256 seed and validates candidates, and a cumulative ledger at /app/solution.json that the agent extends with add_solution.py. The evaluator recomputes A s mod q for every submitted secret and accepts any vector meeting the public alphabet, weight, and residual-bound predicates. Score is 100 times solved instances over 200, as the readme states, on 8 CPU cores with fplll and a 3 hour budget.

Olmo Hybrid, arXiv 2604.03444, motivates the 3:1 Gated DeltaNet reference architecture. The repository ships a locked training and evaluation harness plus reference.py. The agent submits one file, /app/model.py, defining build_model or a NanoSLM class under a 400M parameter cap, optionally declaring a BLOCK_SIZE for training. The judge trains the model from scratch for 900 seconds on one H100 over FineWeb-Edu with the dolma2 tokenizer and measures held-out bits per byte at context 8192. Score is 100 times 2 to the power of minus gamma times val_bpb, normalized so the reference hybrid scores 70, as config.yaml states.

Nano World Models, arXiv 2605.23993, releases a diffusion-forcing video predictor whose Figure 6 shows DDIM step count trading against rollout quality on CSGO. The repository holds a clean checkout at /app/nano-world-model with the frozen NanoWM-L/2 checkpoint. The agent submits a Python-only patch at /app/solution.patch limited to src/diffusion/**.py and src/sample/sampling_utils.py. The judge generates 50 future frames from 4 context images at nominal 50 DDIM steps on hidden episodes on a Modal H100 and measures wall-clock plus LPIPS. Score is clip of 100 log2 speedup times a quality multiplier that stays 1.0 within 3 percent LPIPS tolerance, per the readme, reference 1.17x.

Nano World Models, arXiv 2605.23993, reports that long autoregressive rollouts drift into states that look plausible and are wrong, its Finding 5. The repository holds the same checkout and frozen NanoWM-L/2 CSGO checkpoint. The agent submits a Python-only patch at /app/solution.patch within src/diffusion/**.py and src/sample/sampling_utils.py. The judge runs a long sequential rollout at 50 DDIM steps on a Modal H100 with a horizon drawn per scored run, measures mean LPIPS over the final 20 tail frames, and holds generation time within 10 percent of baseline. Score is 100 times the relative tail-drift reduction times a wall-clock multiplier, per the readme, reference 6.8 percent.

Continuum, arXiv 2511.02230, schedules multi-turn agent requests with job-level FCFS and KV-cache time-to-live so a conversation keeps its prefix resident. The repository holds a pinned upstream vLLM v0.11.0 checkout at /app/vllm. The agent submits a Python-only patch at /app/solution.patch allowlisted to vllm/v1/core/**, vllm/config/scheduler.py, vllm/config/cache.py, and narrow engine, worker, and OpenAI-entrypoint wiring files. The judge serves Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct on one Modal H100 under Poisson arrivals of mini-swe-agent SWE-bench Lite and BFCL memory conversations, gating on greedy token match and per-sample correctness. Score blends clip of 100 log2 geomean latency speedup at weights 0.8 and 0.2 per config.yaml, times an accuracy multiplier.

Li and Yu, PVLDB 17, present SCOPE, a C++ system that computes exact per-vertex orbit counts and shares plans across a batch of queries. The repository holds the stripped artifact at /app with the -b -share path removed. The agent may edit only ten C++ files in counting/, executable/, and plan/. The judge builds scope.out and runs six cases, 4voc and 5voc batches on three graphs, over five rounds, requiring every output file to match the independent path exactly. Score is 25 times the median log2 ratio of independent to candidate wall time, clipped to 100, per the readme.

Xiao et al., Seer, PVLDB 18, accelerate blockchain transaction execution with fine-grained branch prediction in a pre-executing EVM. The repository holds the SeerEVM Go tree and a 353 MiB mainnet snapshot from block 14,650,000. The agent may change only core/vm/predictor.go and must preserve initPredictor, predict, update, and the encodings. The judge replays 200 blocks for development and 400 for grading, scoring only heights 14,650,201 through 14,650,400, and parses per-block branch accuracy B and path satisfaction T. Quality is 100 times 0.8 B plus 0.2 T, and score is 100 times the squared normalized gain over the always-taken calibration, per the readme.

Zhang et al., Spectrum, PVLDB 17, execute consensus-ordered smart-contract transactions concurrently with operation-level rollback through checkpoints of EVM position and stack. The repository holds the Spectrum C++20 tree at /app with the checkpoint-capable stack removed. The agent edits only lib/evmcow/execution_state.hpp, keeping the StackTop, Checkpoint, and ExecutionState interfaces. The judge checks 400-round checkpoint traces against a fixed-array oracle, then drives YCSB, SmallBank, and TPC-C-like generators for one second each and takes median committed TPS. Quality Q is throughput over the cube root of retained memory times latency, and score is clip of 100 log10 of Q_C over Q_B, per the readme.

Arpaci-Dusseau, Zhou, and Chen, PVLDB 18, present ScaleGPM, whose hybrid stage selects between neighborhood sampling and graph sparsification mining engines. The repository holds a reduced artifact at /app minus the threshold selector. The agent supplies a threshold callable in performance_model/src/main.py that reads pattern, error, budgets, cores, and profile attributes and returns GS or NS. The judge replays 112 stored configurations on eight challenge-generated graph profiles, triangle and 4-clique counting at 10 or 20 percent error, and computes geometric-mean regret. Score is 100 times the regret gap below the better constant selector B, divided by B less 1, per the readme.

Bekkers et al., PVLDB 18, engineer the Yannakakis algorithm into a column store by lowering optimizer join trees to two-phase nested-semijoin plans. The repository holds the Python planner modules at /app minus the rewrite policy. The agent implements rewrite_plan in 2phase_nsa/binary_plan/rewrite_policy.py, returning a BinaryJoinNode tree satisfying the lowerability invariant. The judge runs 20 development or 19 graded plans from Stats-CEB, JOB, and a cardinality-estimation benchmark, checks result equality, and times each lowered plan. Score is the mean over queries of clip of 100 log10 of A_q times R_q, the gain over the binary plan and calibrated comparison, per the readme.

SVG-EAR routes video-diffusion attention through sparse strategies with parameter-free linear compensation on the Wan text-to-video path. The repository holds a Git checkout of that path with a pinned Wan2.1 14B checkpoint, the EAR class constructor and three tensor helpers stubbed. The agent edits svg/models/wan/attention.py, svg/kmeans_utils.py, and new modules under svg/solver_extensions/. The judge generates 81-frame 720p videos for four prompts across eight seeds on H100s and measures PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS against dense-attention output plus latency. Score per workload is 100 times a quality factor times 0.25 plus 0.75 times an efficiency value saturating at 2x speedup, per the readme.

BABBLE learns reusable library abstractions from a program corpus using equality saturation and a new e-graph anti-unification method that respects an equational theory. The released Rust repository builds the e-graph, computes anti-unification patterns, extracts compressed programs via targeted beam search, and merges duplicate functions. The task removes the anti-unification and extraction core. Keeping its call sites and declarations. The agent reimplements pattern discovery and compressed-term extraction over the e-graph. The objective is to match or beat the authors on compression ratio and running time across the DreamCoder domains and 2D CAD corpora the paper reports.

Szalinski shrinks unstructured CSG expressions into editable CAD programs with map and fold operators using equality saturation and inverse transformations, a way to speculatively add equivalences to an e-graph. The Rust repository defines the Caddy language in cad.rs and holds the rewrite rules, solver, and permutation logic that drive the search. The task deletes the inverse-transformation and rewrite core that produces smaller equivalent programs. The agent reimplements this search so structured programs fall out of saturation. The objective is to match or beat the authors on program-size reduction and wall-clock time across the CAD models the paper reports.

Polygon generates database inputs that satisfy properties across SQL queries through conflict-driven search over under-approximations of query semantics. The engine encodes lightweight semantic subsets, detects conflicts when an approximation fails, and refines across a family that covers all behaviors of interest, backed by the Z3 solver. The task strips the under-approximation encoding and the conflict-driven refinement loop from the released implementation. The agent rebuilds both so equivalence refutation and disambiguation stay complete. The objective is to match or beat the authors on instances solved and median solving time across the 30,000-plus benchmarks drawn from Calcite, LeetCode, and Cosette.

The egg paper speeds up equality saturation with deferred rebuilding that restores congruence in one amortized pass and e-class analyses that fold domain data into the e-graph. The open-source Rust library implements both techniques and powers case studies on Herbie, linear-algebra optimization, and CAD synthesis. The task removes the rebuilding routine and the e-class analysis machinery. Their interfaces stay wired into callers. The agent reimplements deferred rebuilding and analysis propagation. The objective is to match or beat the authors on the reported speedups, where rebuilding makes congruence about 88 times faster and saturation about 21 times faster.

Ruler infers rewrite rules automatically by enumerating terms into an e-graph, forming candidate equalities, and filtering to a small general ruleset using equality saturation and characteristic vectors. The under-1000-line Rust implementation runs this enumerate, generate, and shrink loop across booleans, bitvectors, and rationals, validating by model checking, SMT, or fuzzing. The task deletes the candidate-generation and rule-selection core. The agent reimplements characteristic-vector matching and derivability-based filtering. The objective is to match or beat the authors, whose rulesets run 25 times faster to synthesize and 5.8 times smaller than the CVC4 baseline at equal proving power.

This work simplifies Mixed Boolean Arithmetic expressions by holding semantically equivalent forms in an e-graph and rewriting toward simpler terms. The implementation uses the egg equality-saturation library to represent and search obfuscated expressions. The task removes the rewrite-and-extract core that recovers a simplified expression from the saturated graph. The agent reimplements the rewrite rules and extraction so deobfuscation still succeeds. The objective is to match or beat the authors on success rate, simplification ratio, and per-expression time across the Tigress, Qsynth, and MBA-Solver benchmarks, where the reported method averages about 0.1 seconds per expression against much slower GAMBA and SSPAM.

Glenside is a pure tensor-program intermediate representation whose access-pattern abstraction lets term rewriting stay layout-aware and sound. Built on the egg library, it maps program fragments to accelerator invocations and discovers layout transformations like im2col automatically. The task removes the access-pattern rewrite rules that drive these transformations. The IR and its callers stay in place. The agent reimplements the rewrites so matrix multiplication, 2D convolution, and max pooling map to hardware calls. The objective is to match the authors by discovering im2col and blocking through equality saturation on the case studies the paper reports.

TenSat applies equality saturation to tensor-graph superoptimization, exploring many equivalent computation graphs at once instead of the order-sensitive sequential rewrites production frameworks use. The Rust implementation builds on egg and extracts an optimal graph with an ILP solver. The task removes the saturation and extraction core, keeping the TASO-derived rewrite rules and cost model. The agent reimplements graph construction and ILP extraction. The objective is to match or beat the authors on runtime speedup and optimization time across BERT, ResNeXt-50, NasRNN, and Inception-v3 on a Tesla T4, where TenSat reaches 16 percent speedup at 48 times less time than TASO.

ACC Saturator optimizes directive-based GPU code by building single-assignment forms, rewriting them exhaustively with equality saturation, and extracting an implementation that cuts computation and memory access. The tool is written in Racket, parses OpenACC and OpenMP through XcodeML, and uses the egg library. The task removes the saturation and extraction stage that rewrites the single-assignment form. The agent reimplements this stage so the emitted kernels stay correct and fast. The objective is to match or beat the authors on execution time and memory throughput across the NAS Parallel Benchmarks and SPEC ACCEL suite on A100 GPUs under the reported compilers.

Spectre shows that speculative execution leaks memory across security boundaries by training branch predictors and reading traces through cache side channels. Variant 1 mistrains a conditional bounds check and variant 2 poisons indirect branches, with secrets recovered through Flush+Reload. The task removes the speculation-gadget and cache-probe core from the proof-of-concept. The harness and measurement scaffolding remain. The agent reimplements the training, transient access, and side-channel readout. The objective is to match the authors by leaking chosen victim memory at the reported rate of roughly 10 KB per second at under 0.01 percent error on the x86 target.

This paper argues that static evaluation overstates LLM defense robustness and that adaptive attackers tuning four optimization families, namely gradient descent, reinforcement learning, search, and human red-teaming, break defenses reported as strong. It attacks twelve jailbreak and prompt-injection defenses across HarmBench, AgentDojo, and OpenPromptInject. The task removes the adaptive attack-construction core. The evaluation harness and defense wrappers stay intact. The agent reimplements the optimization loops that craft defense-specific attacks. The objective is to match or beat the authors on attack success rate, driving most defenses above 90 percent where the original reports claimed near zero.

Progent secures AI agents through privilege control, expressing allowed tool calls as symbolic rules and confining the agent so its action space can only shrink without approval. An LLM drafts and updates policies and an SMT solver classifies each update as narrowing or expanding. The repository holds the policy engine plus the AgentDojo and ASB harnesses. The task removes the policy enforcement and monotonic-confinement core. The agent reimplements rule evaluation and the narrowing check. The objective is to match or beat the authors by cutting attack success rate and preserving task utility on AgentDojo and ASB.

Opal provides private memory for personal AI by confining semantic reasoning to trusted enclaves, so that untrusted disk sees only oblivious accesses through ORAM, backed by an in-enclave knowledge graph and continuous reindexing. The Rust protocol serves controller, embedding, and LLM enclaves over encrypted vector and chunk stores. The task removes the oblivious-access and knowledge-graph query core. The agent reimplements ORAM-backed retrieval and graph filtering. The objective is to match or beat the authors on retrieval accuracy, throughput, and cost against the ANN-only and Graphiti baselines on the synthetic personal-data corpus of 190,000 artifacts and 1,300 queries the paper reports.

This paper introduces Blind Return-Oriented Programming, which exploits a stack overflow in a remote service with no binary or source by observing whether each probe crashes. The attack locates gadgets through stack reads, builds a ROP chain, and writes out the binary to escalate. The task removes the gadget-discovery and chain-construction core. The crash-oracle harness against the server stays in place. The agent reimplements blind gadget finding and chain assembly. The objective is to match the authors by achieving remote code execution on a stack-vulnerable server within the reported few thousand requests and hours-scale time.

Diffusion Policy represents a visuomotor policy as a conditional denoising diffusion process over action sequences, gaining stability and multimodal action handling with receding-horizon control. The released repository separates tasks from methods and defines policy classes including the U-Net image variant plus datasets and environment runners. The task removes the diffusion policy class that predicts action sequences through iterative denoising. The agent reimplements the conditional denoising forward and sampling. The objective is to match or beat the authors on success rate across the 12 tasks in Robomimic, Push-T, Block Pushing, and Franka Kitchen, at the reported 46.9 percent average gain.

MuJoCo Playground is an open-source robot-learning framework built on MJX that trains policies in minutes on one GPU and transfers them zero-shot to hardware. Its stack pairs a physics engine and batch renderer with locomotion, manipulation, and classic-control environments under JAX PPO. The task removes an environment implementation, namely its physics step, reward, and observation logic,. Training scripts stay wired in. The agent reimplements it so a policy trains and transfers. The objective is to match the authors on reward and training time, where most environments finish in under 10 minutes, for tasks like Go1 locomotion and LEAP-hand reorientation.

Raha analyzes wide-area network degradation under failures and traffic shifts by framing the question as heuristic analysis that maximizes the performance gap between the healthy design point and the failed network. The open-source tool encodes the pipeline into the MetaOpt solver backend and clusters the topology to scale. The task removes the gap-encoding and cluster-decomposition core. The agent reimplements the optimization encoding and search. The objective is to match or beat the authors on discovered degradation and run time on the Africa production topology and Topology Zoo networks, finding at least twice the degradation of tools limited to two failures.

Shockwave schedules dynamic-adaptation ML jobs by extending Fisher-market theory to a Volatile Fisher Market and forecasting batch-size changes with Bayesian prediction to maximize Nash social welfare over time. The Python implementation builds on Gavel and includes the scheduler, policy solver, and Accordion and GNS workloads. The task removes the market-solver and prediction core that assigns resources across rounds. The agent reimplements the welfare optimization and the batch-size forecaster. The objective is to match or beat the authors on makespan and worst-case finish-time-fairness, where Shockwave improves makespan 1.3 times and fairness 2 times over Themis, Gavel, and AlloX.

BBQ is a hardware integer priority queue for packet scheduling that ports Hierarchical Find First Set into a pipeline-parallel design, reaching line rate with hundreds of thousands of flows in flight. The repository ships synthesizable SystemVerilog for BBQ and baselines with FPGA and ASIC synthesis scripts. The task removes the bitmapped-bucket enqueue and dequeue logic. The PIFO-style interface and testbench stay in place. The agent reimplements the hierarchical bitmap traversal. The objective is to match the authors, sustaining 100 Gbps line rate on FPGA with over 100K flows and 32K priorities at 300 MHz against the reported baselines.

RedTE performs distributed traffic engineering with multi-agent reinforcement learning so each router acts on local state and reaches near-centralized quality within a sub-100-millisecond control loop. The repository holds the DRLTE agents and an LP solver that computes the optimal reference. The task removes the MARL policy that outputs routing decisions. The simulator, traffic-matrix generator, and LP reference stay in place. The agent reimplements the cooperative agent training and inference. The objective is to match or beat the authors on performance ratio against the LP optimum and on control-loop latency across the GEANT and Abilene topologies the paper reports.

AWQ compresses LLMs with weight-only low-bit quantization, protecting the roughly 1 percent salient channels identified from activation statistics through per-channel scaling rather than mixed precision. The method needs no backpropagation and pairs with the TinyChat kernel runtime. The task removes the activation-aware scale-search and quantization core. Calibration and inference stay wired in. The agent reimplements salient-channel scaling and INT4 quantization. The objective is to match or beat the authors on WikiText-2 perplexity and downstream accuracy at INT4 group size 128 across LLaMA, OPT, and Mistral against the round-to-nearest and GPTQ baselines, with the reported 3-plus times speedup over FP16.

StreamingLLM enables unbounded streaming inference by keeping a few initial attention-sink tokens alongside a rolling window of recent tokens, exploiting the finding that models dump attention onto the first tokens. It needs no fine-tuning and handles millions of tokens. The task removes the sink-plus-window KV-cache management from the attention path. The model and decoding loop stay in place. The agent reimplements sink retention and cache rolling. The objective is to match the authors on stable PG19 perplexity across extended sequences and on the reported speedup of up to 22.2 times over sliding-window recomputation on Llama-2, MPT, and Falcon.

KIVI quantizes the KV cache to 2 bits without tuning, applying per-channel quantization to keys and per-token quantization to values to fit each cache's distribution. The released code integrates the asymmetric scheme into LLM inference. The task removes the quantization and dequantization kernels for both cache halves. The attention and inference path stay wired in. The agent reimplements per-channel key and per-token value quantization. The objective is to match or beat the authors on accuracy across CoQA, TruthfulQA, GSM8K, and LongBench, plus the reported 2.6 times memory reduction and up to 3.47 times throughput gain on an A100.

Hydragen speeds batched inference over shared prefixes by decomposing attention into a shared-prefix term and per-sequence suffix terms, recombining them with log-sum-exp rescaling so prefix attention batches into compute-friendly matrix products. It extends to tree-structured prompt sharing. The task removes the attention-decomposition and recombination core. The inference harness stays in place. The agent reimplements the split prefix and suffix attention and the softmax merge. The objective is to match or beat the authors on throughput with CodeLlama-13b, where Hydragen reaches up to 32 times the vLLM baseline and loses under 15 percent as the prefix grows to 16K tokens.

Wanda prunes LLMs in a single forward pass by removing weights with the smallest product of magnitude and input-activation norm, comparing per output and needing no retraining or weight update. The repository applies this across unstructured and 2:4 and 4:8 sparsity. The task removes the pruning-metric and mask-selection core. Calibration and evaluation stay wired in. The agent reimplements the activation-weighted score and per-output selection. The objective is to match or beat the authors on WikiText perplexity and zero-shot accuracy at 50 percent sparsity across LLaMA and LLaMA-2 against magnitude pruning and SparseGPT, where LLaMA-65B holds dense-level accuracy.

FastV accelerates large vision-language models by observing that image tokens receive little attention in deep layers, so it keeps full attention through early layers and prunes low-ranked visual tokens afterward. With cut layer K equal to 2 and ratio R equal to 50 percent it removes about 45 percent of FLOPs. The task removes the attention-ranking and token-pruning core. The model forward stays in place. The agent reimplements the ranking and drop. The objective is to match the authors on accuracy across A-OKVQA, MMMU, SeedBench, and video QA on LLaVA-1.5, QwenVL-Chat, and Video-LLaVA at the reported FLOP reduction.

DeepCache accelerates diffusion sampling without training by caching high-level U-Net features across adjacent denoising steps and refreshing only low-level features through the skip connections. It composes with DDIM and PLMS samplers. The task removes the feature-cache scheduling and reuse logic. The sampling loop and model stay wired in. The agent reimplements the caching interval and partial-forward reuse. The objective is to match or beat the authors on image quality and speed, where Stable Diffusion v1.5 reaches 2.3 times speedup at 0.05 CLIP-score drop and LDM-4-G on ImageNet reaches 4.1 times speedup at 0.22 FID change across the reported datasets.

Sparse VideoGen2 accelerates video diffusion by clustering tokens with k-means to reorder them by semantic similarity, which sharpens critical-token identification and densifies their layout so sparse attention wastes little GPU work. The training-free method adds top-p budget control and custom kernels. The task removes the semantic-permutation and sparse-attention core. The diffusion pipeline stays in place. The agent reimplements the clustering, reordering, and sparse attention. The objective is to match or beat the authors on PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, and VBench against SVG, SpargeAttention, and XAttention, reaching up to 2.30 times and 1.89 times speedup on HunyuanVideo and Wan 2.1.

Lookahead decoding breaks the sequential dependency of autoregressive generation by trading extra parallel FLOPs to cut decoding steps, generating and verifying n-gram guesses without any draft model and staying compatible with FlashAttention. The task removes the n-gram generation and verification core. The sampling harness stays wired in. The agent reimplements the parallel lookahead and verification branch that preserves the output distribution. The objective is to match or beat the authors on latency across MT-Bench, HumanEval, GSM8K, and ClassEval with LLaMA-2-Chat and CodeLlama, reaching the reported 1.8 times speedup on MT-Bench and up to 4 times on code completion.

SliceGPT compresses transformers post-training by applying orthogonal transformations that leave the network computationally invariant, then deleting rows and columns to shrink the embedding dimension into smaller dense matrices that run on stock hardware. The task removes the invariance-transform and slicing core. Calibration and evaluation stay wired in. The agent reimplements the orthogonal rotation and principal-component slicing. The objective is to match or beat the authors on WikiText-2 perplexity and zero-shot accuracy on PIQA, WinoGrande, HellaSwag, and ARC across LLAMA-2-70B, OPT-66B, and Phi-2, retaining up to 99 percent performance at 25 percent slicing against the SparseGPT baseline.

This work speeds sparse matrix-matrix multiplication by reordering rows and computing cluster-wise with a hierarchical-clustering-based row-clustered format that improves reuse of the second operand and access to the first. The C++ and OpenMP repository holds the clustered formats, hash kernels, and reordering scripts. The task removes the clustered-format construction and cluster-wise kernel. The CSR baseline and drivers stay wired in. The agent reimplements the row-clustered format and its multiply. The objective is to match or beat the authors, reaching about 1.39 times average speedup over Gustavson row-wise hash SpGEMM on 110 SuiteSparse matrices on an AMD EPYC 7763.

Stream-K parallelizes GPU GEMM by splitting the aggregate inner-loop iterations evenly across processing elements rather than assigning output tiles, removing the quantization inefficiency that idles cores on awkward problem shapes. It ships one kernel per precision inside CUTLASS. The task removes the work-decomposition and partial-tile reduction core. The tile machinery stays in place. The agent reimplements the iteration partitioning and cross-block accumulation. The objective is to match or beat the authors across 32,824 GEMM shapes on an A100, where Stream-K averages 1.23 times over CUTLASS data-parallel at FP64 and 1.63 times at mixed FP16 from a single tile size.

KAMI extends communication-avoiding theory inside one GPU with 1D, 2D, and 3D block-level GEMM that uses tensor cores for compute, registers as local memory, and shared memory as the communication medium, targeting small and batched sizes where large libraries fall short. The repository holds the kernels and benchmark scripts. The task removes the CA block-level GEMM kernels. The drivers stay wired in. The agent reimplements the register-and-shared-memory dataflow. The objective is to match or beat the authors in TFLOPS across GH200, RTX 5090, 7900 XTX, and Intel Max 1100, reaching the reported speedups over cuBLASDx, CUTLASS, cuBLAS, and MAGMA.

MIRA is a foundation model for medical time-series forecasting that handles irregular intervals and mixed sampling rates through continuous-time rotary positional encoding, a frequency-specific mixture of experts, and a Neural-ODE extrapolation block for arbitrary timestamps. The repository trains three sizes on a clinical corpus and evaluates zero-shot. The task removes these three blocks. Training and evaluation code stay wired in. The agent reimplements the continuous-time encoding, MoE routing, and ODE extrapolation. The objective is to match or beat the authors on RMSE and MAE across MIMIC, PTB-XL, and held-out datasets, with the reported 10 and 7 percent error reductions.

Zelda is a multi-server preprocessing PIR scheme with unconditional security. The client stores hints from a one-time offline phase and the servers keep only the original database. The Go repository splits into client, server, query, and util packages, and the task removes the client-side hint generation and online lookup logic. The agent must implement those routines so every answer matches the ground truth checked against a seeded database. Scoring compares online response time and client storage with the authors' code, which reports 35ms per query on a 128GB database with 1 kilobyte entries over a simulated 1Gbps link.

QuarterPIR is a preprocessing PIR scheme built from pseudorandom functions alone. It reaches n to the one quarter online bandwidth and square root of n server computation per query, improving on Piano. The Go repository holds a server, the ec24 client that implements the scheme, a Piano baseline, and protobuf messages. The task deletes the ec24 client's preprocessing and online query code and keeps the server and message formats. The agent must rebuild the client so returned entries match the seeded database. Scoring measures online time and bandwidth per query on databases from 1GB to 100GB against the authors' code.

Piano is a single-server PIR scheme with sublinear online computation built from pseudorandom functions rather than homomorphic encryption. The client runs a streaming setup phase and then answers each lookup in amortized work proportional to the square root of the database size. The Go repository contains the server, the client_new implementation, and configuration for entry count and width. The task removes the client's hint construction and online query routines. The agent must restore them so each retrieved entry is correct. Scoring compares query time and client storage with the authors' code, which reaches 12ms per lookup on a 100GB database.

Polar Express approximates the orthogonal factor of a matrix with a fixed sequence of odd polynomial iterations chosen by a minimax criterion, which converges fast and stays stable in bfloat16, replacing Newton-Schulz inside Muon. The repository is a single Python module exposing one function on torch tensors plus a notebook that plots the polynomials. The task deletes the coefficient construction and the iteration loop. The agent must implement both so the output has near-orthonormal columns. Scoring compares approximation error on GPT-2 gradient matrices and final validation loss of Muon training on 1 billion FineWeb tokens against the authors' implementation.

The paper proves that LeJEPA, an alignment objective with a Gaussian regularizer, linearly recovers the latent variables of a world model from nonlinear observations, and shows that no other distribution gives this guarantee. The repository pairs Lean 4 proofs with Python experiments covering 2D mixing functions, latent dimensions up to 1024, and pixel-based control on DMC Reacher. The task removes the loss module that implements the SIGReg and alignment objectives together with the identifiability metrics. The agent must implement them so training recovers the latents. Scoring compares R squared and orthogonality across the released configurations with the authors' numbers.

The Hierarchical Reasoning Model is a 27M parameter recurrent architecture with a slow high-level planner and a fast low-level module that reasons in one forward pass without chain-of-thought data or pretraining. The repository provides pretrain and evaluate scripts, dataset builders for ARC-AGI, Sudoku-Extreme, and Maze-Hard, and the model code under models. The task deletes the two-module recurrent core, its one-step gradient approximation, and the adaptive computation time halting head. The agent must implement these pieces so training runs end to end. Scoring compares exact-match accuracy on Sudoku-Extreme, Maze-Hard, ARC-AGI-1, and ARC-AGI-2 with the authors' checkpoints trained from about 1000 examples.

Mixture-of-Memories gives a linear sequence model several independent memory states and a router that sends each token to a subset of them, which raises capacity and reduces interference at unchanged complexity. The repository implements MoM layers on the Hugging Face stack with training scripts and evaluation harnesses for commonsense and recall-intensive tasks. The task removes the routed layer, including the router, per-state updates, and the shared memory. The agent must implement the layer so models train from scratch. Scoring compares accuracy on FDA, SWDE, SQuAD, NQ, TriviaQA, and DROP at 380M parameters and 15B tokens against the authors' runs.

Nano World Model is a minimalist codebase for video prediction with diffusion forcing that exposes the training target, architecture scale, action injection, and sampling budget as isolated choices. The repository uses hydra configs, ships NanoWM models at several scales, and supports DINO-WM environments, RT-1 robot data, and CS:GO gameplay. The task deletes the diffusion forcing objective and sampler, which assign per-frame noise levels and roll out from a context window. The agent must implement training and sampling so evaluation runs. Scoring compares PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, and FID on RT-1 fractal under the 50K-step ablation protocol with the authors' released numbers.

DFlash accelerates LLM decoding with a lightweight block diffusion drafter that proposes many tokens in one forward pass from hidden features of the target model, which then verifies the proposal in parallel. The repository holds the dflash package with drafter definition, feature extraction, and generation loops for Transformers, MLX, and server backends, plus benchmark scripts. The task removes the drafter and its verification loop. The agent must implement both so outputs stay identical to greedy decoding of the target. Scoring compares speedup and accepted tokens per step on GSM8K, MATH500, HumanEval, MBPP, and MT-Bench with Qwen3-8B against the authors' drafter.

RAGEN trains LLM agents with multi-turn reinforcement learning under StarPO, a trajectory-level optimization framework, and diagnoses the Echo Trap collapse in which reward variance and entropy drop before performance falls. StarPO-S stabilizes training with variance-based trajectory filtering, a critic, and gradient clipping. The repository provides train.py, ten environments with a Gym-style interface, and configs. The task removes the StarPO trainer, including rollout collection, trajectory filtering, and the stabilized policy update. The agent must implement the trainer so runs converge on Qwen2.5 models. Scoring compares success rate on Bandit, Sokoban, FrozenLake, and WebShop with the authors' curves.

JiT trains a plain large-patch Transformer on raw pixels to output the clean image instead of noise or velocity, which lets pixel-space diffusion succeed at patch sizes of 16 and 32 without a tokenizer or auxiliary loss. The repository contains model_jit.py, engine_jit.py, denoiser.py, a training entry point, and FID reference statistics. The task removes the clean-image head and the denoiser that converts its output into a flow for sampling. The agent must implement both so training and sampling run at 256 and 512 resolution. Scoring compares FID and Inception Score over 50,000 generated ImageNet samples with the authors' checkpoints.

Dynamic Tanh replaces normalization layers in Transformers with an element-wise hyperbolic tangent of a learned scalar times the input, and matches or exceeds normalized models across vision, language, speech, and DNA tasks. The repository provides dynamic_tanh.py, ImageNet training scripts, and an other_tasks folder covering MAE, DINO, DiT, LLaMA, wav2vec 2.0, and DNA models. The task deletes the DyT module and the conversion utility that swaps normalization layers for it. The agent must implement both so every configuration trains. Scoring compares ImageNet-1K top-1 accuracy of ViT-B, ViT-L, ConvNeXt-B, and ConvNeXt-L against the authors' reported 82.5, 83.6, 83.7, and 84.4 percent.

CLIPPO trains one Vision Transformer on photographs and on text rendered as pixels with a contrastive loss, so a single encoder handles retrieval, zero-shot classification, and language understanding with half the parameters of CLIP. The code lives in the big_vision repository under configs/proj/clippo with a training config, README, and demo notebook. The task removes the text rendering preprocessing op and the shared-encoder contrastive model definition. The agent must implement them so the config trains end to end. Scoring compares zero-shot ImageNet classification accuracy and image-text retrieval recall with the numbers recorded in the authors' config comments.

The paper shows that sparse Mixture-of-Experts models degrade faster than dense Transformers when training data repeats, with 80M active parameter MoEs suffering at 4 repetitions where their counterparts tolerate 8. It then finds that dropout and masking-based regularization let MoEs beat the baseline past 64 repetitions. No repository is listed, so the task builds on the training stack the authors describe with OLMoE-style data. The task removes the data repetition scheduler and the expert output masking regularizer. The agent must implement both so sweeps over repetition rate run. Scoring compares held-out cross-entropy on the validation domains against the authors' curves.

Agentic Context Engineering improves an LLM system by evolving its prompt as a structured playbook instead of updating weights. A generator produces trajectories, a reflector extracts lessons, and a curator merges them as delta updates with helpful and harmful counters. The repository holds the ace package with these three roles plus evaluation scripts for AppWorld, FiNER, and XBRL Formula. The task removes the reflector and curator, including the deterministic merge logic. The agent must implement them so offline and online adaptation run. Scoring compares AppWorld success and finance accuracy with the authors' reported gains of 10.6 and 8.6 points.

Meta Context Engineering makes prompt optimization learnable with a bi-level system. A meta-level agent refines engineering skills through agentic crossover over the history of executions, and a base-level agent runs the current skill to turn training rollouts into context stored as files and code. The repository provides mce with meta_agent.py and base_agent.py, task environments under env, and scripts for finance, chemistry, medicine, law, and AI safety. The task removes the meta-level agent and its crossover search. The agent must implement it so skills improve across iterations. Scoring compares accuracy on the five domains with the authors' offline and online results.

Meta-Harness optimizes the harness around a language model with an agentic proposer that reads the source code, scores, and execution traces of every earlier candidate. The repository ships two reference examples, a memory-system search for online text classification and a scaffold evolution for Terminal-Bench 2, with a Claude Code wrapper as the default proposer. The task deletes the outer optimization loop that stages candidates, scores them, and exposes the history. The agent must implement the loop so searches run. Scoring compares the best discovered harness with the authors' result of a 7.7 point classification gain at 4x fewer context tokens.

Self-Harness lets a model improve its own agent scaffold. The loop mines weaknesses from execution traces, proposes minimal harness edits tied to those failures, and accepts an edit only after held-in and held-out regression checks pass. The repository contains diagnosis, proposer, acceptance, workflow, and eval directories plus a released Qwen harness. The task removes the weakness mining and proposal modules. The agent must implement them so the loop yields validated edits. Scoring compares Terminal-Bench 2.0 pass rate after self-improvement with the authors' runs, which lift Qwen3.5-35B-A3B from 18.0 to 36.7 and MiniMax M2.5 from 42.2 to 53.9 percent.

SemJoin optimizes semantic joins, which match rows across tables on a natural-language predicate. An LLM advisor routes each query to a classifier strategy for predicates over a discrete label set or to a cluster join that embeds rows, groups both tables, and prunes group pairs by sampling. The repository provides advisor.py, classifier_join.py, cluster_join.py, and evaluation scripts for three datasets. The task removes the advisor and the cluster join with its pruning step. The agent must implement them, and scoring compares F1 and token cost on IMDb reviews, emails, and Stack Overflow tags with the authors' results.

The paper presents a parallel in-place radix sort that models the swaps between array regions as a graph and extracts independent tasks from it, using auxiliary memory logarithmic in the input size. The repository implements the MSD driver in radixSort.h and the method in graphbased.h, with a 2-path variant in edgelistgraph.h and a cycle-finding one in cyclegraph.h. The task removes the graph construction and both global sorting strategies. The agent must implement them so the executables sort correctly. Scoring compares running time on the paper's input distributions against the authors' code, which reports up to 65x speedup on 36 cores.

The paper presents parallel exact and approximate Euclidean DBSCAN algorithms with sequential work bounds and polylogarithmic depth. The repository holds the implementation under code and points to a separate reproducibility repo for datasets. The task removes the clustering computation, namely the grid structure, the core point test, the cell connectivity step, and the approximate variant. The agent must implement them so the output clusters equal the sequential result. Scoring compares running time on the paper's datasets and parameter settings with the authors' code, which reports speedups of up to 33x over the fastest sequential algorithms on 36 cores with hyper-threading.

Hygra extends the Ligra graph framework to hypergraphs and supplies parallel algorithms for betweenness centrality, maximal independent set, k-core decomposition, hypertrees, hyperpaths, connected components, PageRank, and shortest paths. The repository keeps the framework under ligra and the applications under apps/hyper. The task removes the hypergraph traversal primitives that map over vertices and hyperedges and choose between sparse and dense modes. The agent must implement them so all applications compile and return correct results. Scoring compares running time on the paper's hypergraphs against the authors' code, which reports 31x to 53x parallel speedups on 72 cores with hyper-threading.

ParButterfly provides parallel algorithms for butterfly counting per graph, per vertex, and per edge, and for tip and wing peeling in bipartite graphs, with wedge aggregation by sorting, hashing, histogramming, or batching. The repository builds a BipartiteButterflies executable under apps/hyper that selects aggregation and ranking through flags. The task removes the wedge aggregation routines and the peeling loop. The agent must implement them so every countType and peelType option returns correct counts. Scoring compares running time on the paper's real-world bipartite graphs against the authors' code, which reports self-relative speedups of up to 38.5x for counting on 48 cores.

ConnectIt is a framework for parallel connected components that combines k-out, BFS, and LDD sampling with union-find linking and compression schemes to produce several hundred algorithm variants, and it also supports incremental edge insertions. The code lives in the gbbs repository under benchmarks/Connectivity/ConnectIt with framework.h, sampling.h, and per-variant mains. The task removes the sampling strategies and the finish phase that unites the remaining edges. The agent must implement them so every variant returns correct labels. Scoring compares running time on the paper's graphs against the authors' code, which reports an average 12.4x speedup over prior multicore algorithms on 72 cores.
